A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAD neural-network research. Their complete main text, equations, six figures, references, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original experiments on polynomial regression, Heat and Black–Scholes PDE approximation, and MNIST classification.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including loss and parameter-norm trajectories and the MNIST test result.

M1.justification: The network architectures, SAD activation definition, objectives, and GD/Adam training procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate polynomial regression with 1-, 2-, and 4-dimensional inputs, the same Heat and Black–Scholes PDE problems, and MNIST classification.

E2.justification: The same activation-function and GD/Adam comparisons remain in Figures 1–2. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced within the reported experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain the same sampling, batch sizes, architectures, learning rates, metrics, and stopping procedures, including 10,000 polynomial training points and 30,000 MNIST training steps.

E4.justification: The activation/optimizer analyses and Figure 6's rescaling to examine logarithmic parameter-norm growth are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report averaging over 20 independent initializations for polynomial experiments and five for PDE/MNIST experiments. Monte Carlo reference estimation is unchanged, with no new uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The experimental plots in Figures 1–3 and 6 are identical, and their qualitative findings are retained. Appendix E reports the same MNIST test accuracy of 97.93%.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.8(ii) and Corollary 3.6(v) replace a C^1 definable, compactly supported density with a C^1 density whose expected loss is explicitly assumed definable. Appendix B replaces the cited derivation of loss definability with reliance on this assumption. This substantially revises the continuous-distribution hypotheses and proof dependency, while retaining the finite-data results.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 removes 'or even data distribution' from its headline polynomial-divergence contribution. The principal dichotomy, asymptotic optimality, finite-dataset divergence, and empirical claims in the abstract and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Continuous-distribution applicability now explicitly depends on definability of the integrated loss, while compact support is no longer required in the main statements. Experimental interpretations and the practical limitations discussed in Section 1.3 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the implementation details, hyperparameters, sampling instructions, Tesla V100 hardware, and 10–20-minute training-time disclosure. The code and supplementary test-plot access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes Speissegger's 'The Pfaffian closure of an o-minimal structure' (v2 reference 78) and its use in the Theorem 2.8 proof. Other works match across reference renumbering, and the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the contribution paragraph, reorganize the affected theorem statements, and rewrite the definability proof sentence. v3 also adds Allen Gehret to the acknowledgements and updates the version/date stamp; the section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Visual changes are limited to local text reflow and spacing around the revised theorem statements and shortened bibliography. All six figures retain their content, axes, legends, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the definability requirement explicit, improving assumption transparency. However, removing compact support from Theorem 2.8 is not reconciled with its Appendix B proof, which still invokes Corollary A.2's compact-support hypothesis to establish a locally Lipschitz derivative. The finite-data theory and experiments are unchanged. The clearer assumption and newly unresolved proof dependency prevent a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
